newsitem.title: CHINA: China takes new steps to cool heated stocks.
newsitem.headline: China takes new steps to cool heated stocks.

text.p: China took another step to cool its overheated stock markets by announcing on Thursday a sharply expanded quota for new share issues this year.
China will allow 30 billion yuan ($3.6 billion) worth of new stock to be issued this year, twice the quota set for 1996.
The official Xinhua news agency, in its brief announcement, said the quota was aimed at assisting the development of large and medium sized enterprises.
But brokers said stock regulators were eager to cool red hot domestic stock prices that had pushed the nation's stock indices up by more than 50 percent this year.
"This is a much-needed measure to restrain the market," said a broker at Citic Securities in Beijing.
"This will sharply increase the amount of stock available for trading."
Brokers said new shares would absorb liquidity. That would keep traders cautious and place a cap on prices at least over the near term.
The move was also part of a multi-front attack on stock markets that have defied government control.
Last week, the stock transaction stamp tax was increased.
More serious measures were believed to be in progress.
The chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), Zhou Daojiong, was expected to step down soon and an announcement was likely within days, Chinese brokers said.
Brokers said Zhou had reached retirement age and that his removal had been under discussion for months.
Zhou, who was appointed in 1995, was expected to be replaced by Zhou Zhengqing, currently chairman of the Securities Commission under the State Council, or cabinet, they said.
Other top personnel changes were expected at the nation's two stock exchanges in Shanghai and Shenzhen.

In another move to cool the markets, at least four brokerages, including Shenyin & Wanguo Securities, China's largest, would be barred from conducting trading on their own account after irregularities, brokers said.
Asked if Shenyin & Wanguo was among those to be punished, one company official said: "Yes, this is the case."
Officials at J&A Securities and Guangfa Securities confirmed they too would be similarly disciplined.
CSRC officials have declined to comment on the reports.

A previous attempt to end a bull run when the People's Daily, mouthpiece of the Communist Party, issued a harshly worded editorial warning of overheating and a market crash sent prices tumbling and dampened market sentiment for weeks.
